primitives.verbatim_quote: On sample \((p,y)\): - If \(|p-0.5|\ge\delta_j\): **publish**, loss = Brier \((p-y)^2\) - Else: **sit-out**, loss = \(0.25 \approx \mathrm{UNC}\) (coin-flip) Hedge / EG update: \[ w_{t+1,j} \propto w_{t,j}\cdot\exp(-\eta\cdot\ell_{t,j}) \] Regret \(O(\sqrt{T\ln m})\) vs best fixed \(\delta\) in hindsight.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When |p - 0.5| < δ_j, expert sits out, assigning zero loss but signaling low confidence.

reasoning_traces.think:
The adaptive delta hedge operates by allowing each expert to set a personal threshold δ_j, which determines whether their prediction should be published. If |p - 0.5| ≥ δ_j, the prediction is published with Brier loss (p - y)^2; otherwise, it is ignored with a fixed loss of 0.25 (representing coin-flip uncertainty). The Hedge algorithm updates expert weights using exponential gradient descent, minimizing regret compared to any fixed threshold in hindsight. This structure enables a dual mechanism: one that dynamically filters predictions based on confidence, and another that learns optimal thresholds from past performance. The integrity check ensures that when predictions are frequently ignored due to low confidence, this signals either poor skill or sufficient data to raise the threshold. The regret bound O(√T ln m) guarantees that the cumulative loss remains close to the best fixed δ in hindsight, making the system robust to adversarial environments. The interplay between these components allows for both adaptive filtering and principled learning of optimal publishing criteria.
